validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: high confidence. P3493 (Urengoy-Petrovsk) is independently confirmed as a real, major, named Gazprom trunk gas pipeline by (1) proektirovanie.gazprom.ru's own design-institute encyclopedia (names it among 'crupnykh' gas pipelines the institute worked on) and (2) Seligman's Cambridge PhD thesis (Cambridge University, agricultural/geography dept, 1999), which independently discusses it throughout Ch.2 as one of the 'six Siberian gas pipelines' of the UGSS export system, with compressor-station counts (24), construction methods and completion timeline. No duplicate-row or misattribution risk found -- P3493 is the only GEM row for this route. SPEC: the thesis's completion-year evidence (1981, cited twice from the same underlying Soviet trade-press source) conflicts with the sheet's recorded StartYear1=1983; no source found anywhere in this pass that supports 1983. This is flagged as a spec concern rather than silently corrected because it traces to a single source lineage (both citations derive from 'Stroitel'stvo Truboprovodov' 1986/1994) -- a second, independent confirmation of either year would resolve it. Diameter (1420 OD / Ду1400) and Length (2733 vs 2726-2730) both check out within the established DN/OD and rounding conventions used elsewhere in this same batch (P0756) -- not concerns.

Could not find a source stating a 32 bcm/y capacity figure specifically for Urengoy-Petrovsk. Searched the Seligman thesis (gives lengths, compressor-station counts and completion dates for this line but no throughput/capacity number), the Kazan-tr and Pomary Gazprom-encyclopedia pages (neither states capacity), and a targeted web search for Russian-language capacity figures (no per-line number surfaced; only whole-corridor or system-level aggregates). NOTE for plausibility only (not a citation): 32 bcm/y is close to the P3507/P5612 design rate of 89 mill.Sm3/day (~32.5 bcm/y) for the same-era, same-diameter (1420mm) sibling lines in this corridor, so the recorded value is not implausible -- but this is reasoning, not a source, and is left UNRESOLVED.
